title: MOFA sincerely thanks Belize and Paraguay for firm support in defiance of authoritarian intimidation; welcomes US opposition to China’s coercion
text:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) strongly condemns a recent announcement by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs imposing sanctions on Belizean Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade Francis Fonseca and Paraguayan Minister of Information and Communications Technologies Gustavo Villate. The measures demonstrate the authoritarian nature of China’s intimidation. MOFA once again firmly rejects China’s blatant interference in the sovereignty and foreign policies of other nations and its violation of the principles of international law.

In defiance of China’s coercion and threats, Belizean Prime Minister John Briceño, Minister Fonseca, Minister Villate, and the foreign ministries of both countries all stated that they would continue to stand with Taiwan. They underscored that Belize and Paraguay were sovereign, independent nations and reiterated that the right of states to conduct their own diplomatic affairs was a matter of international consensus and common principle. The Belizean and Paraguayan people also voiced their support for maintaining diplomatic relations with Taiwan. MOFA is deeply grateful to the governments and peoples of Belize and Paraguay.

In addition, the US Department of State underlined its commitment to standing with its friends and partners, including Taiwan, to advance shared prosperity, security, and democratic values. It expressed its opposition to coercion and aggression by China against countries in the Western Hemisphere for exercising their sovereign rights, demonstrating that the United States is moving forward together with Taiwan, Belize, Paraguay, and other members of the free and democratic community.

MOFA reiterates the following: the ROC (Taiwan) is a sovereign and independent country; neither it nor the People’s Republic of China is subordinate to the other; China has no right to interfere in Taiwan’s diplomatic relations; and China’s deplorable suppression of Taiwan, Belize, and Paraguay will only draw international derision.

Taiwan maintains strong partnerships with both Belize and Paraguay. Long-term cooperation in a diverse range of areas—including agricultural and fisheries technology, infrastructure, health care, trade and investment, higher education, and social welfare—has yielded remarkable results. Collaboration continues to deepen and strengthen. The administrations and high-level officials of Belize and Paraguay have strongly supported Taiwan at the United Nations General Assembly and other international organizations.

Having stood together through thick and thin, the countries share a profound friendship. Taiwan will continue to work closely with Belize and Paraguay to pursue mutually beneficial development and coprosperity, jointly resist China’s global authoritarian expansionism, and defend the universal values of democracy, freedom, human rights, the rule of law, and the right of peoples to self-determination. (E)
